issues.detail: The Greek 'ουδ αν' (neither if/nor if) implies a conditional hypothetical ('neither would he be...'). The Vietnamese 'chẳng phải là' (is not) renders it as a flat statement of fact. The Greek structure suggests that IF He were on earth, He would NOT be a priest because there are already priests; the Vietnamese makes it sound like a current state of being.

The Greek 'οντων' (being/existing) is a participle describing the priests. The Vietnamese 'vì đã có' (because there are already) changes the grammatical relationship from a description of the priests' status to a causal reason for why He isn't a priest.
